Compressed Texture Write Inefficiency.name: Compressed Texture Write Inefficiency
Compressed Texture Write Inefficiency.description: Measures the overhead from scattered writes to compressed textures. When writes are scattered, the GPU must read the existing block, decompress it, modify the affected pixels, recompress, and write it back. When writes cover a full block, the GPU can simply compress and write directly to memory. A value of 0% indicates all writes are efficient (full-block writes). A value of 100% indicate all writes are scattered. When the inefficiency is high, compression degrades performance rather than helping it. To optimize, restructure writes to cover complete blocks rather than individual scattered pixels.

L1 Cache Pressure Influence Normalized.description: The L1 Cache Pressure Influence metric describes the way in which the Occupancy Manager Target is influenced due to (non-GPR) pressure within the Apple GPU L1 caches at a given point in time. When this metric is non-zero, it typically denotes that the current working set is too large to fit into the Apple GPU L1 caches efficiently, and/or the L1 caches are experiencing a high number of evictions (i.e thrashing). A lower metric value equates to a higher amount of pressure within the Apple GPU L1 caches. The GPU believes it may be beneficial to decrease the total active number of SIMDGroups for more optimal cache behavior. If this Influence metric is seen to be major influence on occupancy manager target and is unexpectedly limiting the overall Occupancy, it is recommended to analyze the workload’s private L1 memory cache bandwidths and residency around the problem area.

Texture Stalls Influence Normalized.description: The Texture Decompression Stalls Influence metric describes the way in which the Occupancy Manager Target is influenced due to texture decompression stalls within the Apple GPU caches at a given point in time. When this metric is non-zero, it typically denotes that the GPU is not able to keep up with the number of texture sample requests that are occurring. The metric value is proportional to the amount of stalling within the Apple GPU texture caches. The GPU believes it may be beneficial to decrease the total active number of SIMDGroups for more optimal cache behavior. If this Influence metric is seen to be driving the Occupancy Manager Target low and unexpectedly limiting the overall Occupancy, hiding latencies between texture samples may provide performance gains. It may also be useful to explore disabling settings such as allowGPUOptimizedContents usage flag on the problem texture(s). See https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/optimizing-texture-data for more details. To confirm if enabling texture compression is counter productive take a look at 'Compression Ratio of Texture Memory Read' counter track

Memory Request Stalls Influence Normaliz.description: The Memory Request Stalls Influence metric describes the way in which the Occupancy Manager Target is influenced due to graphics memory stalls within the Apple GPU caches at a given point in time. If its value is non-zero it means memory requests are causing stalls in the memory hierarchy including GPU last level cache, MMU and main memory. The GPU believes it may be beneficial to decrease the total active number of SIMDGroups for more optimal cache behavior. If this Influence metric is seen to be driving the Occupancy Manager Target to be low and unexpectedly limiting the overall Occupancy, use strategies to reduce random memory access patterns to large buffers, use texture compression and texture mipmapping to reduce memory traffic.
